scope: Exploit serializer divergence to hide an allergen, cross-branch leak via raw query, missing snapshot on legacy orders
method: adversarial read-only attempt — exhaust attack surface on the 3-resources + items-board service path

attack_vectors.title: Allergen hiding via items-board serializer omission — chef relying on items-board column for prep batching sees no allergen warning
attack_vectors.scenario: Customer A orders Cheeseburger with allergen 'gluten'. Customer B orders Cheeseburger no allergen. POS captures allergens_snapshot=['gluten'] for A, [] for B. KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService::orderItems() correctly splits them into 2 KDS lines (allergen-hash split, verified by sentinel KdsAllergenAggregationSplitTest). BUT the serialized payload via KDSOrderItemsResource ships ZERO allergen info to the frontend. The items-board template doesn't currently render allergens, so the chef preps a 'Cheeseburger x2' card if they group by item-name in their head, missing the allergen flag entirely. The today-orders card view DOES surface the allergen via KDSOrderDetailsResource → OrderItemResource, so the warning exists somewhere on the screen — but the items-board column is silently allergen-blind.
attack_vectors.exploit_result: Real-world risk: chef in rush only checks items-board column → misses allergen on a card → gluten contamination. Probability bounded by chef workflow (they're trained to check both views) but the serializer SHOULD ship the field as defense-in-depth. Confirms Z-1 finding. RECOMMENDATION: heal inline.
attack_vectors.blocked_by_existing: Partial — today-orders card surface DOES render allergens; items-board column does NOT. Defense exists but not on both surfaces.

attack_vectors.title: Cross-branch leak via raw query manipulation on items-board endpoint
attack_vectors.scenario: Staff with branch_id=5, JWT token signed legit. Sends GET /admin/kds-order/items?branch_id=1 hoping the controller forwards branch_id to the service. Or sends ?branch_id=0 hoping to gain admin scope.
attack_vectors.exploit_result: BLOCKED. KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService::orderItems() (lines 257-331) reads $userBranchId = auth()->user()->branch_id ?? 0 — NEVER from request. The orderFilter array (line 36-43) allows request-side branch_id only in list() not in orderItems(). orderItems() has no request param processing at all beyond auth user. BranchScope auto-applied on OrderItem model as defense-in-depth. Cross-branch leak impossible via items-board endpoint.
attack_vectors.blocked_by_existing: Two layers — explicit auth()->user()->branch_id resolution + BranchScope global on Order AND OrderItem.

attack_vectors.title: Allergen-hash collision via crafted unicode in allergens_snapshot — could merge two distinct allergen sets into one line
attack_vectors.scenario: Legacy order has allergens_snapshot=['gluten ', ' gluten'] (with whitespace). Service normalizeAllergensForHash applies array_filter(value !== null && value !== '') but does NOT trim() per-element. sha1 would yield different hash than ['gluten'].
attack_vectors.exploit_result: PARTIAL EXPLOIT. If POS code or migration backfill emits ['gluten '] with trailing space, the hash differs from ['gluten'], splitting lines that should merge (food-safety SIDE: chef sees 2 cards instead of 1 — safer not less-safe). The defense err on the side of split (more cards, never fewer). NOT a food-safety bug, but a usability inefficiency.
attack_vectors.blocked_by_existing: Conservative split-on-difference is food-safety-positive even when hash mismatches are spurious.
attack_vectors.fix_class: BACKLOG V1.0.X — normalize trim() in normalizeAllergensForHash

attack_vectors.title: Missing snapshot on legacy orders pre-2026_04_18 backfill — fallback path serves empty allergens
attack_vectors.scenario: Order created before backfill migration 2026_04_18_140004 + 2026_04_20_131600 ran. allergens_snapshot is NULL.
attack_vectors.exploit_result: MITIGATED. BackfillAllergensSnapshotCommand exists (app/Console/Commands/BackfillAllergensSnapshotCommand.php) and the service normalizeAllergensForHash collapses null/empty to identical hash. Resource fallback returns []. Wire shape is consistent. The customer who placed a pre-backfill order without an allergen profile gets a card without allergen flag — which is correct (no allergen recorded).

attack_vectors.title: Composition snapshot tampering attempt — frontend re-sends order with crafted composition_snapshot to bypass server-side pricing
attack_vectors.scenario: Adversary client sends item_id + a fabricated composition_snapshot pre-baked with extras=0 prices. Tests if backend trusts the snapshot from request.
attack_vectors.exploit_result: BLOCKED at order creation (PricingService is SSOT — composition_snapshot is COMPUTED by the backend at create-time and stored frozen, not read from request). Once stored, the snapshot is what KDS reads — and there is no KDS endpoint that mutates orders' composition_snapshot. The /change-status endpoint mutates only status field. Wire-immutable post-create.
attack_vectors.blocked_by_existing: Pricing SSOT NF525 invariant + KDS endpoints are read-only on snapshot.

attack_vectors.title: Resource null-pointer crash via deleted Item — items-board references $this->orderItem?->name with null-safe op
attack_vectors.scenario: Item soft-deleted post-order. OrderItem relation Order::orderItem withTrashed (model:91), so the relation resolves to the soft-deleted Item. Resource ships item_name safely.
attack_vectors.exploit_result: DEFENDED. withTrashed() on the orderItem relation + null-safe operator $this->orderItem?->name. Result: soft-deleted items keep their name on KDS, chef sees a coherent card.

attack_vectors.title: Replay attack: re-POST identical /change-status with stale expected_status
attack_vectors.scenario: Adversary or buggy client re-submits status change after a peer already advanced the order.
attack_vectors.exploit_result: BLOCKED by optimistic locking (KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService::changeStatus:189-202) — DB lockForUpdate + expected_status check + 409 on conflict. Logged for telemetry. No state corruption.

p1_findings: PK-3-RED-01 — confirms Z-1 allergen contract gap
summary.all_other_attacks: BLOCKED by existing defenses (BranchScope, NF525 SSOT, optimistic lock, defensive null-safety, conservative hash-split)

verdict.summary: Defense surface is solid across cross-tenant, replay, and tamper vectors. The single confirmed P1 is the Z-1 allergen contract gap, which is HEAL-ALLOWED scope and trivial 1-line fix. No P0 found. Items-board endpoint is the weakest contract by accident of historical drift, not by adversarial vulnerability.
verdict.heal_recommended: YES — PK-3-RED-01 + PK-3-ARCH-01 are the same finding (Z-1 confirmation). Apply minimal fix + sentinel test.
